title: Flash Sale Fail
covers: finding the percent of a number using part = percent × base, fixing the whole-number percent error, and comparing discounts
cert: finding and comparing percents of numbers using decimals and equations

intro.caption: Lesson 4-4 — find and compare with percentages. Ruben ran the flash sale numbers on the register, and somehow a 30% discount made a $70 sneaker cost MORE than $70. Time to rescue the sale.

balloons.t: Uh, guys? Our 30% off flash sale just charged Cole $2,100 for a $60 cap!
I knew we should have let Hye-jin touch the register.
Always turn the percent into a decimal first! 30% is 0.30, not 30.
And the base is the number right after "of." Multiply them to get the part.
Okay, 30% is 0.30. Then 5% must be 0.5, right?
No! 0.5 is 50 percent. Five hundredths is 0.05!
40% off a $45 shoe sounds huge. Is it better than 25% off an $80 shoe?
Don't guess by the percent alone! Different bases change the dollar discount.
Here's a deal: 15% off my $200 rare kicks. That's $15 off, right?
Wait a second — 15% of $200 is NOT $15! Check him, Hye-jin!
Every price tag fixed, zero $2,100 caps, and Sly got out-calculated.

win.caption: To find the percent of a number, change the percent to a decimal (divide by 100) and multiply by the base: part = percent × base.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Percent of a Number
gates.prompt: Convert each percent to a decimal first, then multiply by the base to find the discount.
hints: Conceptual: the base is the original price right after "of," and a percent is hundredths of that base.
Procedural: divide the percent by 100 to make a decimal, then multiply decimal × base.

items.aria: thirty percent discount on a sixty dollar cap

fb.msg: $42 is the sale price left after subtracting. Here we only want the discount.
30 is the percent itself, not 30% of $60.

items.label: A hoodie costs $90 and is 15% off. Discount = ($)
items.aria: fifteen percent discount on a ninety dollar hoodie

fb.msg: $9 is 10% of $90. Add another 5% ($4.50) to get 15%.

gates.pass: $18 off the cap and $13.50 off the hoodie. The register is starting to make sense.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Fix Ruben's Math
gates.prompt: Spot the place-value mistakes in Ruben's register entries and fix them.
hints: Conceptual: multiplying by 30 instead of 0.30 makes the answer 100 times too big. Single-digit percents like 5% are 0.05, not 0.5.
Procedural: move the decimal point two places left to turn any percent into a decimal.

items.q: A $70 sneaker is 30% off. Ruben typed 30 × 70 = 2,100. What is the real discount?

options.fb: 30% is 30/100 = 0.30. Multiplying by 30 makes the discount 100 times too big!

items.label: Tax on a $40 tee is 5%. Someone typed 0.5 × 40 = $20. Real tax = ($)
items.aria: five percent tax on a forty dollar shirt

gates.pass: $21 off and $2 tax! Ruben tapes "MOVE DECIMAL 2 LEFT" onto the register.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Compare Deals
gates.prompt: Compute each discount with its own base before comparing, then find a final sale price.
hints: Conceptual: a smaller percent of a bigger base can save more money than a bigger percent of a smaller base.
Procedural: compute part = percent × base for each deal, and subtract the discount from the original price for the sale price.

worked.q: Which saves more: 10% off $90 or 25% off $32?

items.q: Deal A: 25% off $80. Deal B: 40% off $45. Which deal saves more money?

options.t: Deal B always wins because 40% is bigger than 25%
options.fb: The bases are different ($80 vs. $45). Compute both dollar discounts first!

options.t: Deal B saves $18, which is more than Deal A's $20
options.fb: Check the numbers: $20 is more than $18!

options.t: Deal A saves $20, which is more than Deal B's $18

items.label: A $120 jacket is 20% off. Sale price after the discount = ($)
items.aria: sale price of a one hundred twenty dollar jacket at twenty percent off

fb.msg: $24 is the discount taken off. Subtract $24 from $120 to get the sale price!
$100 subtracts 20 as dollars instead of 20% of $120.
$144 added the $24 discount instead of subtracting it!

items.fbDefault: First find the discount: 0.20 × 120 = $24. Then subtract from $120.

gates.pass: Deal A wins ($20 vs. $18), and the jacket rings up at $96!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Rescue the Sale
gates.prompt: Fix the last two price tags and expose Sly's $200 sneaker math.
hints: Conceptual: always check that your decimal matches hundredths (35% = 0.35, 8% = 0.08).
Procedural: multiply decimal × base for every tag.

items.label: Tag 1 · Find 35% of $80. ($)
items.aria: thirty five percent of eighty dollars

items.label: Tag 2 · Find 8% of $150. ($)
items.aria: eight percent of one hundred fifty dollars

items.q: Final Check · Sly offers 15% off $200 and says "That's $15 off." What is the real discount?

options.fb: 15% of $100 is $15, but here the base is $200!

gates.pass: BEEP! $28, $12, and $30! The flash sale is saved and Sly's suitcase snaps shut.

journal.heading: Lesson 4-4 — what the flash sale fail taught us
rows: part = percent × base. The base is the whole right after the word "of."
Always divide the percent by 100 before multiplying: 30% = 0.30, and 5% = 0.05 (never 0.5).
A bigger percent of a small price can save less than a smaller percent of a big price.
Multiplying by 30 instead of 0.30 makes a $60 cap cost $2,100.
journal.quote: "Move the decimal two places left, or you owe me two thousand bucks." — Cole

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 4-4 (Find and Compare with Percentages) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers part = percent × base, converting percents to decimals, and comparing discounts across different bases.
standards: Find the percent of a number using an equation or model, and compare percents of different bases
